discoveries.headline: Russia opens bitcoin to everyday investors, with a cap
discoveries.why: Since 17 November, ordinary Russians can buy bitcoin, ether and Tether's USDT through licensed brokers, but only up to 300,000 rubles (about US$3,600) a year per intermediary, and only after passing a test. Olivia Stephanie at crypto.news explains the rest: exchanges could start trading from 22 November with central bank approval, the Moscow Exchange plans to begin on 1 December, and paying for everyday goods in crypto stays restricted. A clear look at how a big economy is bringing crypto inside tight rules. Education, not advice.
discoveries.meta_credit: crypto.news · Olivia Stephanie, edited by Rony Roy

discoveries.headline: Europe's leaders meet to argue over money and Ukraine
discoveries.why: EU leaders gather in Brussels for a special summit on a seven-year budget worth almost €1.7 trillion, which some say is too much and others too little. Euronews' team sets out what else is on the table: a €45 billion support loan for Ukraine, financed through joint debt, that a few member states want to opt out of, and the race for the next head of the European Central Bank. A quick way to understand the deals that will shape Europe for years.
discoveries.meta_credit: Euronews · Jorge Liboreiro, Luca Bertuzzi and colleagues

discoveries.headline: Two new howler monkeys, found in their genes
discoveries.why: Scientists from the University of Salford and the University of Gothenburg have named two new species of howler monkey from the Amazon, Alouatta iroi and Alouatta matogrossensis, by reading the genomes of 11 howler species. Great rivers like the Amazon, Xingu and Rio Branco kept populations apart long enough to become separate species, and one of the two lives in southern Amazonia, one of the world's fastest-deforesting regions. As Romina Batista puts it, knowing which species exist is the first step to protecting them.
discoveries.meta_credit: University of Salford · study in Communications Biology, led by Romina Batista with Jean Boubli
discoveries.credit: Photos: John Trent (CC BY-NC-ND) and Bruno Rennó

discoveries.headline: Thupten Jinpa on the courage to be kind
discoveries.why: Thupten Jinpa, the Dalai Lama's English translator since 1985, talks with James Shaheen and Sharon Salzberg about why compassion is part of our basic nature, and why it takes a little courage to live by it. Turning toward others with warmth is one of the surest ways the Dalai Lama's tradition offers to loosen stress and find steady happiness, and Jinpa closes with a short guided meditation. A kind way to start the day. Free from Tricycle's Life As It Is podcast.
discoveries.meta_credit: Tricycle · Life As It Is, with James Shaheen and Sharon Salzberg

discoveries.headline: When a new country starts to feel like home
discoveries.why: A five-month stay in Berlin turned into nearly nine years, and in this short Psyche essay the writer traces how that changed their sense of self and of home, and why feeling at home somewhere new can make you a stranger in the old place. Anyone who has moved, or loves someone who has, will recognise it. Eleven minutes, just right for the commute (Psyche's audio uses AI narration of the human-written essay).

discoveries.headline: Northlane's Anemoia lands today
discoveries.why: Australian band Northlane release their seventh album, Anemoia, today, a record that leans into trance and electronic sounds from the 1990s and early 2000s. Singer Marcus Bridge tells Sarah Duggan at The AU Review how it grew from a planned five-track EP, how he treated his voice like "another texture and another layer", and why the tour has moved to May 2027. A good day to give it a first listen.

discoveries.headline: Five ways to longer life in mice share one molecule
discoveries.why: University of Michigan researchers tested five treatments known to lengthen mouse lives, including calorie restriction and the drug rapamycin, and found they all raised the same antioxidant, ergothioneine, found notably in mushrooms. Newsweek's Melissa Fleur Afshar lays out the study in Frontiers in Aging, and the experts' caution: it is mostly male mice, a long way from a human therapy, and as one says, "a fingerprint isn't a finish line". General information, not medical advice.

discoveries.headline: Fifteen minutes of vinyasa for hips and back
discoveries.why: Teacher Jessica Haessly guides a 15-minute practice to strengthen and free up the hips, back and spine, using lying, seated and face-down postures and a single block. It works as a warm-up before a longer flow or as a short morning ritual on its own. Free on Insight Timer.

discoveries.headline: Over 55? You can choose a gentler lift and still get stronger
discoveries.why: In a small University of Western Australia pilot trial, adults over 55 picked either high-intensity or low-to-moderate resistance and impact training, twice a week with supervision. After 12 weeks both groups grew significantly stronger on the leg press and chest press, so the right intensity may be the one you will keep coming back to. Check with your clinician before starting a new program.
discoveries.meta_credit: EurekAlert! · research by Brett D. Buist and colleagues, The University of Western Australia
